self_monitoring.reason: A finite record cannot naively contain a final cryptographic hash of its own completed bytes without changing those bytes.
self_monitoring.next_generation_rule: The next journal entry MUST retrieve this committed genesis entry, record its Git identity/content hash, compare it with the expected committed generation, and classify the result.

recursive_test_rule.statement: Every finalized observatory result, baseline, correction, receipt, and journal entry becomes an eligible subject of later drift checks.
recursive_test_rule.anti_circularity: Recursive monitoring is provenance evidence only; it is not counted as independent replication of an anomaly.

journal_invariants: history is append-only in logical meaning
corrections are new records rather than silent replacement
each non-genesis entry references and verifies the previous committed entry
the live branch may advance but pinned historical generations are expected to remain stable
a broken chain is R9 unless explicit repository history explains it

minimum: at least one later retrieval time T1
check live main and map ordinary changes to commit history
capture raw SHA-256 for external static controls when possible
record any newly admitted external live subjects before inspecting them for drift
